judged_text: When credential sharing is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from the sync endpoint, but this call site types the result as HubspotToken and reads hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token and hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in, which are not properties of a Response. The first Hubspot token refresh in sharing mode reads undefined refresh_token/expires_in from the Response object, produces a NaN/undefined expiry, and hands a Response to code that expects a parsed HubspotToken — the Hubspot integration breaks for synced users on its first refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, the function performs a `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, but in sharing mode that value will actually be a `Response`, not a `HubspotToken`. Any subsequent reads like `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token` / `hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in` will be `undefined`, causing incorrect expiry computation and breaking the HubSpot refresh flow for synced users on first refresh.
